hints.title: Height-Balanced Root Partition Obstacle
hints.text: To produce a height-balanced search tree from sorted elements, subtree heights cannot differ by more than one. Which element from the sorted sequence must be chosen as the subtree root to balance children evenly?

hints.title: Median Split Invariant
hints.text: Choosing the exact middle element of any subarray as the root partitions the remaining elements into two equal halves, ensuring minimal height difference.

hints.title: Recursive Midpoint Construction Procedure
hints.text: Define a recursive helper taking subarray bounds [left, right]. If left > right, return null. Compute mid = (left + right) // 2. Create a TreeNode with nums[mid]. Recurse on [left, mid - 1] for left child and [mid + 1, right] for right child. Return the node.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of nums array (1 <= N <= 10^4)
complexity.notes: Visiting each array element once and creating nodes in O(log N) balanced recursion stack depth.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Iterative left-to-right insertion creates a degenerate linear tree of depth N.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(log N) call stack memory, optimal for balanced tree creation.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Using mid = (left + right) // 2 to guarantee balanced subtrees.
